summary: Before an OLD strict-config binary rollback, remove claude_primary_ownership and claude_primary_ownership_observe. Prepare default-off stricter primary-Claude ownership (real installed topology remains unverified), isolating a Claude seat's channel and hooks from nested Claude processes, and retain automatic channel-recovery attempts across brief replacement success.

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rebuild.

schema.detail: No database schema, replicated claim format or migration changes. Explicitly opted-in new Claude generations retain an additive local process-generation witness alongside their existing harness ownership.

rules.detail: No claim vocabulary or admission-rule change. Existing fenced runtime actions and mailbox epochs remain in use.

compatibility.detail: New install settings claude_primary_ownership and claude_primary_ownership_observe are both absent/false by default. The separate observe setting only opts this daemon into bounded, non-authorizing legacy topology capture; absent/false schedules no capture, inventory or blocking-pool task and does not imply enforcement. Only enforcement true opts fresh claims in. The owning daemon supplies that install choice to a fresh wrapper claim; only explicit true mints an ownership witness. Off keeps legacy admission, including after a natural restart. Existing protected generations retain their recorded choice across driver reexec; turning the setting off affects only a subsequent authorized fresh launch and never interrupts a live seat. Older strict config readers reject either new key, so remove BOTH keys BEFORE rolling back the binary. The direct-parent rule is a NEW restriction compared with the old any-descendant Linux admission; a legitimate launcher shim could be falsely refused, so enabling it requires accepted topology evidence and separate rollout authority. The source default does not enable it. Darwin is UNQUALIFIED until its existing hosted macos-ci lane executes the real child-chain controls. Nested channels serve an unscoped MCP protocol and cannot bind a protected primary seat; nested hooks cannot publish its native-session or observation state. Nested-Claude isolation is restart-gated and opt-in: it protects only wrappers freshly claimed with that install setting enabled. Deploying the binary alone does not mint records on subsequent launches. Existing wrapper generations without a witness retain legacy admission until their next natural authorized restart; doctor reports those seats as unprotected without replacing their independently established delivery readiness or binary freshness. Consumers identify unprotected ownership through the reason text, not delivery state=legacy; a ready current-image seat can report state=current while unprotected and passes the deployments delivery-health gate, which does not certify ownership protection. Consequently, upgrading only the daemon does NOT protect the person's currently running legacy seat and the present symptom can continue until a separately authorized natural wrapper launch. Explicitly enabled legacy shadow decisions only describe sampled topology and never change admission or recovery. An unavailable proof on an established stream holds new effects without disconnecting it or charging automatic recovery; delivery stays unknown, surfaced as suspect after three checks with bounded diagnostics, until proof succeeds or a proven mismatch/actual disconnect ends the stream. Old daemons ignore the additive witness. The automatic replacement start reason now identifies automatic recovery instead of explicit intent; mixed fleets retain the old reason text from old members.

manual.detail: No agent conduct, environment stripping or tool restrictions. Protection requires separately reviewed explicit install opt-in and a future authorized fresh wrapper launch; this change authorizes neither.

recovery.detail: NEW visible recovery policy: only new requests stamped with the versioned existing operation value spend this budget; adoption does not inherit prior restart attempts or their park faults, which remain visible history. Old pending automatic requests retain their existing action semantics and automatic initiator; this is not observational-only daemon adoption. Automatic success does not erase attempts. Three automatic channel-recovery restart attempts within a persisted rolling six-hour window park channel recovery with its existing owner-visible fault; explicit authorized restart or expiry reopens the budget. Parking targets only its recorded incarnation. Existing explicit restart and required deployment paths remain available. An OLD binary treats the stamped operation as non-recovery, hence an explicit budget reset: rollback reopens the old budget (more automatic restarts allowed) and uses the old generic explicit reason text. No mixed-version policy guarantee is claimed.

downtime.detail: Source qualification does not authorize interrupting an active seat or establish installed-process remediation. Kernel and synthetic controls require ordinary hosted qualification.
